sections.sectionText: 2nd-8 weeks. Exploring St. Louis: This course provides career and RST industry exploration. Students will develop networking skills, while engaging with RST industry alumni and professionals in their offices, agencies, and facilities. Best practices and current issues will be explored. Students will have the potential to make connections for future internships and career advancement. Potential site visits and networking opportunities could include St. Louis Cardinals (MLB), St. Louis Blues (NHL), St. Louis City Soccer Club, St. Louis University athletics and campus recreation facilities, St. Louis Union Station, Ballpark Village, and America’s Center Convention Complex. Exact dates of the two-day trip are TBD. Course includes a $160 fee, to cover hotel and transportation. In addition, there will be three one-hour class times scheduled with the trip. Attendance at the meetings is mandatory. Please contact Jason Schroeder (schroe24@illinois.edu) for further information. *Eligible for the RST Minor: http://catalog.illinois.edu/undergraduate/ahs/minors/recreation-sport-tourism/

1st 8-weeks. Course will examine historical foundations and contemporary challenges emanating from athletic programs operating within higher education institutions. An analysis of relevant literature and current media accounts, along with a dialogue from industry leaders will provide a unique insight to the expectations facing the next generation of collegiate administrators. Topics include: Historical Foundations of Intercollegiate Athletics; Fan Engagement in the Evolving Sport Landscape; NCAA Governance Models / Contemporary Issues; Name, Image, & Likeness & the role of the Collective Organization; Financial Management / Capital Programs; Perspectives on Media Rights; Equity Issues and College Athletics; and, Organizational Management Strategies. Students who have completed RST 199 MR (Issues in Sport & Higher Education) should not register for RST 204. While the number is different, the course content is the same. Registering for the new course would be seen as duplicate credit. Duplicate credit does not count toward graduation, and students registering for the duplicate course will be asked to drop. *Eligible for the RST Minor:

sections.sectionText: Students participate in practicum positions at University-approved sites. The practicum course is a 1-credit course that requires you to complete a minimum of 100 hours with an agency that relates to the field of recreation, sport, and tourism. The course enhances the practicum experience by leading you through practical steps that empower you in the learning/working experience. The Job Description must be approved and Site Confirmation Form and Affiliation Agreement must be in place prior to the start of the practicum experience. Contact the practicum coordinator for specific instructions 3-weeks prior to the start date. Both the agency and the University provide supervision. Coursework required for credit of course. 1 undergraduate hour. Approved for S/U grading only. Prerequisite: Instructor Approval Required

subject: RST
title: Experiencing Agritourism
info: Same as ACE 280. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.

sections.sectionText: Combining in-class and site visits, this course explores business, policy, and marketing aspects of “farm to fork” and “seed to glass” agritourism enterprises. Course content emphasizes issues of environmental sustainability, social and cultural impacts, and community and economic development. Through this course, students will build capacity for critical thinking and problem-solving skills within the context of agritourism, event and outdoor recreation management. COURSE INCLUDES off campus site visits to agritourism locations and organizations. Meets with RST 593 EA and ACE 280 EA. Students who have completed RST 199 EA (Experiencing Agritourism) should not register for RST 290. While the number is different, the course content is the same. Registering for the new course would be seen as duplicate credit. Duplicate credit does not count toward graduation, and students registering for the duplicate course will be asked to drop. *Eligible for the RST Minor: http://catalog.illinois.edu/undergraduate/ahs/minors/recreation-sport-tourism/
